questions.q: The “fight-or-flight” response is primarily mediated by which division of the autonomic nervous system?
questions.explanation: The sympathetic nervous system mediates the stress response.

questions.q: The main function of platelets (thrombocytes) is:
questions.explanation: Platelets are essential for primary haemostasis (clot formation).

questions.q: A patient’s laboratory results show elevated BUN and creatinine. The nurse suspects dysfunction of which organ?
questions.explanation: BUN and creatinine are waste products normally excreted by the kidneys; elevated levels indicate renal impairment.

questions.q: A patient with increased intracranial pressure (ICP) has an ICP reading of 25 mmHg. The nurse should:
options: Elevate the head of the bed to 30 degrees
Position the patient flat to increase cerebral perfusion
Administer a bolus of normal saline
questions.explanation: Normal ICP is 5–15 mmHg. HOB elevation to 30 degrees promotes venous drainage and helps reduce ICP.

questions.q: A patient is receiving a blood transfusion. Fifteen minutes after starting, the patient reports chills, low back pain and feels "something is wrong." The nurse's priority action is to:
options: Slow the transfusion rate and give diphenhydramine
Stop the transfusion and keep the IV line open with normal saline
Complete the transfusion and monitor vital signs
Administer acetaminophen and continue the transfusion
questions.explanation: These symptoms suggest a hemolytic transfusion reaction. The transfusion must be stopped immediately and the line kept open with saline.

questions.q: The nurse is caring for a patient with a chest tube to water seal drainage for a pneumothorax. Continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber indicates:
options: An air leak in the system
The chest tube needs to be removed
questions.explanation: Continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber indicates an air leak. Intermittent bubbling with exhalation or coughing is normal.

questions.q: The water seal chamber of a chest tube drainage system should be kept:
options: At the level of the patient's head
Below the level of the patient's chest
At the level of the patient's heart
Above the patient to promote drainage
questions.explanation: The drainage system must be kept below the level of the chest to promote gravity drainage and prevent backflow.

questions.q: A patient undergoing mechanical ventilation has an endotracheal tube cuff pressure of 35 cm H₂O. The appropriate action is to:
options: Document the finding as within normal range
Notify the respiratory therapist to adjust cuff pressure to 20–30 cm H₂O
Increase the cuff pressure to prevent aspiration
questions.explanation: Normal ETT cuff pressure is 20–30 cm H₂O. Higher pressure increases the risk of tracheal ischemia and necrosis.

questions.q: A patient has a pulmonary artery (Swan-Ganz) catheter. The pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) reflects:
questions.explanation: PAWP reflects left atrial pressure, which approximates left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LV preload).

questions.q: A patient is admitted with a traumatic brain injury. Cushing's triad includes:
questions.explanation: Cushing's triad (late sign of raised ICP) includes hypertension with widening pulse pressure, bradycardia and irregular respirations.

questions.q: The most reliable indicator of pain in a non-verbal, intubated patient is:
options: Behavioral pain assessment tools (e.g. CPOT, BPS)
Family report of the patient's usual pain responses
questions.explanation: Validated behavioral pain assessment tools (CPOT, BPS) are the standard for assessing pain in non-verbal intubated patients.

questions.q: A postoperative patient has a PCA pump with morphine. The patient is sleeping with a respiratory rate of 8 breaths per minute. The priority action is to:
options: Place the patient in high Fowler's position
Stop the PCA infusion and administer naloxone as ordered
Increase the oxygen flow rate to 4 L/min
Shake the patient vigorously to arouse
questions.explanation: Respiratory rate of 8 indicates opioid-induced respiratory depression. Stop the PCA and give naloxone.

questions.q: A patient on a ventilator has oxygen saturation dropping to 88%. The nurse's priority action is to:
options: Check the ventilator connections and circuit
questions.explanation: For acute desaturation, first increase FiO₂ to 100% to provide immediate oxygenation while assessing the cause.

questions.q: A patient with a tension pneumothorax following chest trauma would present with:
options: Hypotension, jugular venous distension, absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation
Hypertension, flat neck veins, bilateral breath sounds
Bradycardia, warm dry skin, symmetrical chest expansion
questions.explanation: Tension pneumothorax presents with hypotension, JVD, absent breath sounds on the affected side and tracheal deviation away from the affected side.

questions.q: During the immediate postoperative period, the nurse's priority assessment is:
options: Patency of the airway and quality of respirations
questions.explanation: Airway patency and respiratory status are the highest priority in the immediate postoperative period (ABCs).

questions.q: A patient is admitted with full-thickness burns to the anterior trunk and both anterior thighs. Using the Rule of Nines, the estimated burn size is:
questions.explanation: Anterior trunk = 18%, each anterior thigh = 9%. Total = 18% + 18% = 36%.

questions.q: In a patient with hemorrhagic shock, vasoconstriction occurs due to activation of:
options: Baroreceptor reflex via the vagus nerve
Sympathetic nervous system and adrenal medulla
questions.explanation: Hemorrhagic shock activates the sympathetic nervous system and adrenal medulla, releasing catecholamines that cause systemic vasoconstriction.

questions.q: The priority nursing diagnosis for a patient immediately following a major burn injury is:
options: Risk for infection related to skin barrier loss
Impaired physical mobility related to pain and edema
Deficient fluid volume related to increased capillary permeability
Imbalanced nutrition: less than body requirements
questions.explanation: In the emergent phase (first 24–48 hours), fluid loss from increased capillary permeability makes deficient fluid volume the priority.

questions.q: A patient with a newly placed tracheostomy is being suctioned and oxygen saturation drops to 85%. The priority action is to:
options: Complete the suction pass to clear the airway
Remove the suction catheter and administer oxygen
Instill 5 mL of normal saline before the next pass
questions.explanation: If oxygen saturation drops during suctioning, remove the catheter immediately and administer oxygen. Limit each pass to 10–15 seconds.

questions.q: A patient is prepared for elective surgery. Which medication increases surgical bleeding risk and should be reported?
questions.explanation: Aspirin increases bleeding risk and is typically held 5–7 days before surgery.

questions.q: A patient with a spinal cord injury above T6 is at risk for which complication when a noxious stimulus is present?
questions.explanation: Autonomic dysreflexia is a medical emergency that can occur with spinal cord injuries at or above T6 in response to a noxious stimulus (usually bladder or bowel).

questions.q: A patient with Guillain–Barré syndrome is most at risk for which life-threatening complication?
questions.explanation: Ascending paralysis can involve the respiratory muscles, leading to respiratory failure that may require mechanical ventilation.

questions.q: A patient with myasthenia gravis is experiencing a myasthenic crisis. The priority nursing concern is:
options: Respiratory muscle weakness and airway protection
questions.explanation: Myasthenic crisis causes severe muscle weakness that can include the respiratory muscles, threatening the airway.

questions.q: A patient with acute pancreatitis is most likely to have which laboratory finding?
questions.explanation: Serum amylase and lipase are typically elevated in acute pancreatitis.

questions.q: A patient with cirrhosis and ascites is scheduled for a paracentesis. The nurse should monitor most closely for which complication after the procedure?
questions.explanation: Removal of large volumes of ascitic fluid can cause a rapid fluid shift and hypovolemia.

questions.q: A patient with chronic heart failure is prescribed digoxin and furosemide. The nurse should be most alert for signs of:
questions.explanation: Furosemide causes potassium loss. Hypokalemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity.

questions.q: A patient with a suspected basilar skull fracture should not have which procedure performed?
questions.explanation: Nasogastric tubes are contraindicated in basilar skull fractures because of the risk of intracranial placement.

questions.q: A patient with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is most likely to have which finding?
questions.explanation: A hallmark of ARDS is refractory hypoxemia that does not improve adequately with increasing oxygen concentration.

questions.q: A patient with a history of chronic alcohol use is admitted with confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia. The priority medication to administer is:
questions.explanation: This presentation suggests Wernicke’s encephalopathy. Thiamine should be given before or with glucose to prevent worsening of the condition.

questions.q: A patient with a newly diagnosed deep vein thrombosis is started on heparin infusion. The nurse should monitor which laboratory value to guide therapy?
questions.explanation: Unfractionated heparin therapy is monitored using aPTT.

questions.q: A patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is receiving oxygen at 2 L/min via nasal cannula. The nurse understands that higher oxygen flow rates may:
options: Suppress the hypoxic drive to breathe in some patients
Have no effect on respiratory drive
questions.explanation: Some COPD patients rely on hypoxic drive. Excessive oxygen can reduce their respiratory drive.

questions.q: A patient develops sudden shortness of breath, chest pain and anxiety while receiving a central line insertion. The nurse suspects:
questions.explanation: Air embolism is a risk during central line insertion or disconnection. The patient should be placed in left Trendelenburg position if air embolism is suspected.

questions.q: A patient with a history of heart failure reports waking up at night short of breath. This symptom is known as:
questions.explanation: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea is sudden nighttime breathlessness that wakes the patient and is classic in heart failure.

questions.q: A patient with acute kidney injury has a serum potassium of 6.8 mEq/L and ECG changes. The nurse anticipates which urgent treatment?
options: Calcium gluconate, insulin with glucose, or other potassium-lowering measures
questions.explanation: Severe hyperkalemia with ECG changes requires immediate measures to stabilize the cardiac membrane and shift or remove potassium.

questions.q: The condition for which a nurse prepares a woman for emergency caesarean delivery is
questions.explanation: Cord prolapse is an obstetric emergency requiring immediate CS if vaginal delivery is not imminent. Meconium alone or non-reactive NST are not absolute indications for emergency CS; twins are often managed according to presentation and gestation.

questions.q: To screen for the presence of neural tube defects in the fetus, the test that would be performed on a pregnant woman is
questions.explanation: Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (MSAFP) is the primary screening test for neural tube defects. Amniocentesis is diagnostic; BPP and TORCH are not NTD screens.

questions.q: During first examination of normal newborn baby, a nurse would expect to identify
options: Umbilical stump that has two veins and one artery
Eye discharge that is yellow and watery
Hands and feet that have a bluish color
Apical pulse rate of 90 beats per minute
questions.explanation: Acrocyanosis (bluish hands/feet) is normal in the first 24–48 h. Umbilical cord normally has two arteries and one vein; yellow watery eye discharge is abnormal; normal newborn apical rate is 120–160 bpm.

questions.q: A laboring woman’s husband assists her during the transitional phase of labor. The behavior that if exhibited by the husband would require intervention by a nurse is
options: Provides effleurage when the woman complains of intense abdominal pain
Gives ice-chips when she says her mouth is dry
Offers bed pan when she needs to have a bowel movement
Encourages her to fix gaze on him during contractions
questions.explanation: Offering a bedpan when the woman feels the urge to defecate may encourage bearing-down before full dilatation and risks cervical oedema or fetal injury. Ice chips, effleurage and focal point are appropriate support.

questions.q: When assessing a woman who is 20 weeks pregnant, the nurse would expect the uterine fundus to be at
options: Midway between symphysis pubis and umbilicus
Midway between umbilicus and xiphoid process
questions.explanation: At approximately 20 weeks the fundus reaches the umbilicus. At 12 weeks it is at the symphysis; midway symphysis–umbilicus is ~16 weeks.

questions.q: A primigravida in active labor (8 cm dilated) starts pushing. During the next contraction the nurse should
options: Deep breath, hold, and bear down
Apply firm pressure on lower back
questions.explanation: At 8 cm the cervix is not fully dilated; the woman should pant with short rapid breaths and not push. Directed prolonged pushing is reserved for second stage.

questions.q: The midwife should suspect pregnancy-induced hypertension if she finds
questions.explanation: Pregnancy-induced hypertension / pre-eclampsia is defined by new-onset hypertension plus proteinuria after 20 weeks.

questions.q: The treatment of puerperal mastitis before suppuration occurs is
options: Antibiotics, incision and drainage, breast support
Antibiotics, breast support and heat application
Antibiotics, breast support and ice application
questions.explanation: Before abscess formation: antibiotics, continued breastfeeding/expression, breast support and local heat. Incision & drainage only after fluctuance/abscess.

questions.q: In focused antenatal care
options: The mother is encouraged to decide on place of birth when labor begins
The mother is encouraged to visit antenatal clinic at least seven times during pregnancy
The mother is encouraged to save money for baby clothes
The mother is encouraged to make transport arrangements several months before delivery
questions.explanation: Focused antenatal care emphasises birth preparedness, including transport arrangements well before labour. Place of birth is planned in advance, not decided when labour starts.

questions.q: Exhibitionism
options: Is intensified when the perpetrator has excess free time and is under significant stress
Occurs equally in both men and women
Is more frequent in men without satisfying sexual relationships
questions.explanation: Exhibitionism occurs predominantly in men and is associated with unsatisfactory sexual relationships; the behaviour is recurrent over ≥6 months.

questions.q: The activities the nurse engages in during the preparatory phase of home visit includes
questions.explanation: Preparatory phase of a home visit includes clarifying the reason/source of referral and planning the visit.

questions.q: A contact disease caused by bacteria is
questions.explanation: Impetigo is a bacterial contact disease. Pediculosis and scabies are parasitic; trachoma is chlamydial but classically eye-to-eye.

questions.q: Some of the indirect client services provided by the community health nurse include
questions.explanation: Indirect community health nursing services include record-keeping and supervision of care provided by others.

questions.q: When fetal head is well flexed, the presenting diameters are
questions.explanation: Well-flexed vertex: sub-occipito-bregmatic (9.5 cm) and biparietal (9.5 cm) diameters.

questions.q: The muscle layer involved in enmeshing bleeding vessels and preventing bleeding after delivery of placenta is
questions.explanation: The middle (oblique) layer of myometrium acts as living ligatures around vessels after placental separation.

questions.q: During the 2nd trimester of pregnancy, the blood pressure falls due to
options: Effects of progesterone on smooth muscles causing relaxation and dilatation of arterial wall
Effects of oestrogen on smooth muscles causing relaxation and dilatation of arterial wall
Effects of progesterone on smooth muscles causing relaxation
Effects of oestrogen on smooth muscles causing relaxation
questions.explanation: Progesterone causes smooth-muscle relaxation and vascular dilatation, contributing to the mid-pregnancy fall in blood pressure.

questions.q: At the end of pregnancy the total weight gain is expected to be approximately 12 kg
questions.explanation: Major contributors to the ~12 kg average weight gain are the fetus and maternal fat stores.

questions.q: The following are possible signs of pregnancy except
options: Presence of human chorionic gonadotrophin in blood or urine (positive pregnancy test)
questions.explanation: Positive signs of pregnancy are fetal heart sounds, ultrasound visualisation and palpation of fetal parts. Presence of hCG is a probable sign.

questions.q: The minor disorders of pregnancy that may progress to major complications include
questions.explanation: Severe/persistent nausea and vomiting can progress to hyperemesis gravidarum; constipation and heartburn are usually milder.

questions.q: Over delegation involves
options: Transferring too much roles from the manager to the subordinates
Delegating at the wrong time, to the wrong person for the wrong reasons
questions.explanation: Over-delegation is transferring excessive responsibility/roles to subordinates.

questions.q: The trophoblast cells of the developing zygote form the
questions.explanation: Trophoblast cells form the placenta and chorion.

questions.q: In focused antenatal care, the second dose of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) is administered at gestation of
questions.explanation: In the older focused-ANC schedule used in many Kenyan exams, the second dose of IPTp-SP is given at 28–34 weeks (current WHO: every ANC contact from 13 weeks, ≥1 month apart).

questions.q: If Mrs. Cola’s menstrual period was on 27.7.08, her expected date of delivery will be
questions.explanation: Naegele’s rule: LMP 27 July 2008 → +9 months = 27 April 2009 + 7 days = 4 May 2009.

questions.q: The diastolic pressure is usually not affected by excitement; its increase is therefore more significant in assessment of pregnant women for pre-eclampsia. The range of change in mmHg is
questions.explanation: A rise in diastolic pressure of 15–20 mmHg (or absolute ≥90 mmHg) is clinically significant in the assessment of pre-eclampsia.

questions.q: Fetal axis pressure is more significant during
options: Active and second stages of labour when membranes are ruptured
Second stage of labour when membranes are intact
Early stages of labour transmitting force to upper pole of fetus
Second stage transmitting force to lower pole of uterus
questions.explanation: Fetal axis pressure becomes effective once the membranes are ruptured in active labour and second stage.

questions.q: If membranes rupture at cervical dilation of 8 cm, a vaginal examination should rule out
options: Cord prolapse, cord presentation, fetal distress
Obstructed labour, cord prolapse, fetal compromise
Obstructed labour, prolonged labour, cord presentation
Maternal distress, prolonged labour, cord presentation
questions.explanation: Immediate vaginal examination after rupture of membranes at advanced dilatation is performed to exclude cord prolapse/presentation.

questions.q: The partograph is an effective tool in management of labour; good progress in active phase will be
options: Cervical dilatation plotted progressively on alert line within 7 hours
Uterine contractions increasing in strength within 8 hours
Cervical dilation plotted on action line with progressive descent
Cervical dilation plotted to the right of action line
questions.explanation: Good progress in active phase is cervical dilatation progressing on or to the left of the alert line.

questions.q: The initial characteristics of rigid cervix in cervical dystocia include
questions.explanation: Cervical dystocia: cervix remains thick, oedematous and unyielding despite contractions.

questions.q: After birth, the functional closure of ductus arteriosus takes place within
questions.explanation: Functional closure of the ductus arteriosus occurs within 12–24 hours after birth (anatomical closure later).

questions.q: Mrs Dodo, para 6+0, at six weeks postnatal clinic demands bilateral tubal ligation; the midwife should
options: Take in-depth medico-social history and encourage partner participation
Reassure and encourage lactational amenorrhea method
Schedule return date for preparation of procedure
Check pregnancy test then provide method
questions.explanation: Before bilateral tubal ligation a thorough history and partner involvement/counselling are required.

questions.q: The exogenous causative organisms of puerperal infection include
questions.explanation: Exogenous puerperal infection is classically associated with haemolytic streptococci (and other organisms introduced from outside).

questions.q: Injury to the fetal scalp due to pressure by girdle of contact is known as
questions.explanation: Caput succedaneum is soft-tissue swelling of the scalp caused by pressure against the cervix/girdle of contact; it crosses suture lines and resolves quickly.

questions.q: Fetal causes of early pregnancy loss include
options: Infections such as rubella, listeria and chlamydia
Structural abnormalities of the genital tract
questions.explanation: The commonest fetal cause of early pregnancy loss is chromosomal abnormality of the conceptus.

questions.q: The outcome of labour is not dependent on
options: Degree of moulding of the fetal head
questions.explanation: Outcome of labour depends primarily on powers, passenger and passage; absolute maternal size alone is not the determinant.

questions.q: In monitoring fetal well-being using the fetal kick chart, you will tell the client to notify you if she counts
questions.explanation: Classic fetal kick-chart advice: notify if fewer than 10 movements are felt in 3 hours (or per local protocol).

questions.q: The part of the uterus in which a contraction begins is
questions.explanation: Uterine contractions begin in the fundus and spread downward.

questions.q: Uterine contractions are controlled by the
questions.explanation: Uterine smooth muscle is under autonomic (mainly hormonal) control.

questions.q: The volume of amniotic fluid after 20 weeks gestation is
questions.explanation: Amniotic fluid volume after 20 weeks is typically 750–800 ml (peaks later around 800–1000 ml).

questions.q: The hormone that maintains endometrium and stimulates maternal metabolism and breast alveoli development during pregnancy is
questions.explanation: Progesterone maintains the endometrium, supports maternal metabolism and prepares breast alveoli.

questions.q: During pregnancy, the glomerular filtration rate
options: Makes most dramatic changes near birth
questions.explanation: GFR rises substantially in pregnancy (by ~50%).

questions.q: The mechanism of labour that allows the fetal head to present itself to fit the widest anteroposterior diameter of the pelvic cavity is
questions.explanation: Flexion presents the smallest diameters (sub-occipito-bregmatic) to the pelvic inlet.

questions.q: Closure of the newborn’s foramen ovale occurs when
options: Left atrial pressure exceeds right atrial pressure
Blood flows from pulmonary artery to aorta
questions.explanation: Foramen ovale closes when left atrial pressure exceeds right atrial pressure after the first breaths.

questions.q: The newborn with post-maturity syndrome is at high risk for cold stress due to
questions.explanation: Post-mature infants have reduced subcutaneous fat and are at high risk of cold stress.

questions.q: Presence of meconium in the newborn’s lungs
options: Traps inspired air in the alveoli
questions.explanation: Meconium can cause ball-valve obstruction, trapping air and leading to air leaks/atelectasis.

questions.q: Symptoms of superficial thrombophlebitis include
options: Local redness and tenderness in a portion of the vein
Edema of ankle and lower leg
Pain in affected leg and foot
questions.explanation: Superficial thrombophlebitis: local redness, warmth and tenderness along a superficial vein.

questions.q: Direct causes of placental abruption include
options: Abnormally short umbilical cord, sudden loss of uterine volume
Defective vascularization of decidua, previous uterine surgery
Injury to abdomen from fall or accident, multiple pregnancy
questions.explanation: Direct mechanical causes of abruption include short cord and sudden uterine decompression.

questions.q: The hormones produced by the ovary include
questions.explanation: Ovary produces oestrogen and progesterone (and small amounts of relaxin/androgens).

questions.q: In the uterus the fetus is protected against ascending infection by
questions.explanation: The operculum (‘show’) and cervical mucus plug protect against ascending infection.

questions.q: During early development, the fetal kidney begins to function and can pass urine between
questions.explanation: Fetal kidneys begin to function and produce urine around 8–12 weeks.

questions.q: During pregnancy, increased plasma volume leads to
questions.explanation: Expanded plasma volume dilutes haemoglobin → physiological anaemia of pregnancy.

questions.q: Positive signs of pregnancy include
options: Ultrasound and palpation of fetal parts
Fetal heart sounds and softened uterus
questions.explanation: Positive signs include ultrasound visualisation and palpation of fetal parts (and fetal heart sounds).

questions.q: The expected date of delivery of a mother whose LMP was 24.9.2013 is
questions.explanation: LMP 24 Sept 2013 → EDD 1 July 2014 (Naegele).

questions.q: In a singleton pregnancy, the fundal height reaches the level of the umbilicus at
questions.explanation: Fundus at umbilicus at 20–22 weeks in a singleton.

questions.q: Engagement occurs when
options: The widest diameter of the presenting part enters the pelvis below the pelvic inlet
The oblique diameter passes through the brim of the pelvis
Widest occipito-posterior diameter passes through pelvic outlet
Transverse diameter passes through pelvic cavity
questions.explanation: Engagement = widest diameter of the presenting part has passed through the pelvic inlet.

questions.q: During physiological changes in first stage of labour, formation of retraction ring is followed by
options: Formation of upper and lower uterine segment
questions.explanation: Formation of the retraction ring is associated with differentiation of upper and lower uterine segments.

questions.q: During labour, emotional support is best provided by
options: Single quiet room and procedure explanation
questions.explanation: Continuous support by a companion plus clear explanations is the most effective emotional support in labour.

questions.q: Fetal distress occurs when the fetus
options: Suffers oxygen deprivation and becomes hypoxic
Does not breathe immediately after birth
questions.explanation: Fetal distress = fetal hypoxia/oxygen deprivation.

questions.q: During second stage of labour, internal rotation of the head is followed by
questions.explanation: After internal rotation of the head, extension occurs under the pubic arch.

questions.q: In the second stage of labour the midwife should
options: Take fetal heart after every contraction
Do vaginal examination to rule out cord prolapse
questions.explanation: In second stage fetal heart is auscultated at least every 5–15 minutes (or after each contraction in high-risk).

questions.q: Immediately after head has crowned the midwife should
questions.explanation: Immediately after crowning, check for nuchal cord.

questions.q: Direct causes of maternal mortality are
questions.explanation: Direct obstetric causes of maternal death include PPH and puerperal sepsis (also eclampsia, obstructed labour, unsafe abortion).

questions.q: Lactational amenorrhea method of family planning is suitable for a woman who
options: Breastfeeds exclusively, has not resumed menstruation, baby less than 6 months
Wants protection, resumes menstruation after six months, breastfeeds on demand
Breastfeeds exclusively, has delayed menstruation, baby more than 6 months
Breastfeeds exclusively, has not resumed menstruation, wants highly effective method
questions.explanation: LAM criteria: exclusive breastfeeding, amenorrhoea, infant <6 months.

questions.q: Handicaps classified as mental handicap include
questions.explanation: Mental handicap examples include conditions such as Down syndrome (mongolism) and sequelae of meningitis/birth injury affecting cognition.

questions.q: The following symptoms in a pregnant woman is of most concern
questions.explanation: Visual disturbance is a danger sign of severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia and requires urgent attention.

questions.q: A 21-year-old pregnant woman diagnosed with hyperemesis gravidarum is pre-exposed to;
questions.explanation: Hyperemesis gravidarum predisposes to electrolyte imbalance and dehydration.

questions.q: Rh isoimmunization in pregnancy develops when;
options: Rh-ve fetal blood crosses into maternal blood
Rh+ maternal blood crosses into fetal blood
Rh+ fetal blood crosses into maternal blood stimulating antibodies
Rh-ve fetal blood crosses into maternal blood
questions.explanation: Rh isoimmunisation: Rh-positive fetal blood enters Rh-negative maternal circulation and stimulates antibody formation.

questions.q: Maternal and fetal blood exchange occurs mainly at;
questions.explanation: Maternal and fetal blood do not mix under normal conditions; exchange occurs across the placental membrane.

questions.q: Caput succedaneum is correctly described as;
options: Scalp tissue swelling over presenting part
questions.explanation: Caput succedaneum is scalp oedema over the presenting part that crosses suture lines and resolves in days.

questions.q: Pulsating tissue felt during vaginal examination indicates;
options: Leave finger in place and call for help
questions.explanation: Pulsating tissue is the umbilical cord. Do not remove the examining fingers if they are elevating the presenting part off the cord; call for help immediately and prepare for emergency delivery/CS.

questions.q: Leading cause of maternal death in Kenya is;
questions.explanation: Haemorrhage remains the leading direct cause of maternal death in Kenya.

questions.q: Postnatal daily observation includes;
questions.explanation: Daily postnatal observations include perineum, vital signs and uterine involution.

questions.q: Watching a nursing video indicates psychomotor level;
questions.explanation: Watching a demonstration video corresponds to the acquisition level of the psychomotor domain.

questions.q: Hypokalemia means low;
questions.explanation: Hypokalaemia = low serum potassium.

questions.q: Preoperative tumor shrinking chemotherapy is;
questions.explanation: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy is given before surgery to shrink the tumour.

questions.q: For a woman who is in labor and experiencing slight shoulder dystocia the nurse would
options: Apply fundal pressure to the suprapubic area
Obtain an order for oxytocin infusion
questions.explanation: For mild shoulder dystocia: McRoberts manoeuvre + firm suprapubic pressure (NOT fundal pressure). Fundal pressure is contraindicated. Knee-chest is used for cord prolapse.

questions.q: The following should be highly considered when counseling family planning and HIV positive clients
options: Drug interactions between hormonal methods and anti-tuberculosis drugs
The client’s current stage of AIDS
The client’s economic status and source of funding
questions.explanation: Rifampicin and other enzyme-inducing TB drugs reduce efficacy of combined hormonal contraceptives; dual protection or alternative methods are required.

questions.q: When preparing a family for their parent’s changed role due to HIV status an important aspect to consider is
questions.explanation: Destigmatisation is central when helping a family adapt to a parent’s HIV diagnosis.

questions.q: Mini, a 7-year-old boy diagnosed with ADHD. The drug group most likely to be used would be
questions.explanation: First-line pharmacotherapy for ADHD is CNS stimulants (methylphenidate, amphetamines).

questions.q: Benzhexol (Artane)
options: May be used safely in patients with prostatic hypertrophy
Should never exceed 15 mg daily dosage
Should not be administered to patients with Parkinsonian syndrome
questions.explanation: Benzhexol (trihexyphenidyl) daily dose is usually limited (commonly ≤15 mg); higher doses increase anticholinergic toxicity. It is used in Parkinsonism and is relatively contraindicated in prostatic hypertrophy.

questions.q: The group A drugs recommended by WHO for the treatment of Gonorrhoea include
questions.explanation: WHO first-line for uncomplicated gonorrhoea: ceftriaxone 250–500 mg IM (plus azithromycin for dual therapy). Spectinomycin is alternative.

questions.q: The immediate treatment for an infant with severe diarrhea and sunken eyes and fontanelles includes
options: Giving intravenous fluids and then admit
Giving an anti-diarrhoeal drug and admit immediately
Taking a blood slide for malarial parasites and then admit
Giving oral rehydration solution plus an antibiotic
questions.explanation: WHO Plan C for severe dehydration: rapid IV rehydration (e.g. 30 ml/kg then 70 ml/kg) then reassess; antibiotics only if indicated.

questions.q: The management of hypotonic uterine action includes
options: Intravenous infusion of syntocinon in normal saline
Intravenous infusion of syntocinon in 5% dextrose
questions.explanation: Hypotonic uterine action is augmented with oxytocin (syntocinon) infusion, classically in 5% dextrose in many Kenyan protocols (modern practice also uses saline).

questions.q: The management of placenta previa type three when the fetus has died in utero includes
options: Induction of labour by use of syntocinon
Preparation of woman for emergency caesarean section
Gentle palpation through vaginal fornices to determine position
Complete bed rest and speculum examination on third day
questions.explanation: Type III placenta praevia with intrauterine fetal death is still managed by caesarean section because of the risk of catastrophic haemorrhage.

questions.q: The hormonal factors responsible for uterine contractions at onset of labour are
options: Optimum levels of estrogen and rise of prostaglandins in maternal circulation
Increased release of oxytocin progesterone from decidua at term
Formation of oxytocin and estrogen in fetal circulation
Rise of oxytocin and estrogen in fetal circulation
questions.explanation: Onset of labour is associated with rising oestrogen relative to progesterone and increased prostaglandin production.

questions.q: At primary level of anti-retroviral prophylaxis for PMTCT, a HIV-positive woman should take
options: Nevirapine 200 mg at onset of labour
Nevirapine 300 mg at onset of labour
Zidovudine 2 mg/kg within three days of delivery
questions.explanation: Older PMTCT protocols used single-dose nevirapine 200 mg at onset of labour (current Kenya guidelines favour lifelong ART for all pregnant women living with HIV).

questions.q: The anti-opioid drug used in resuscitation of the newborn is
questions.explanation: Naloxone (Narcan) 0.1 mg/kg IV/IM is the opioid antagonist used in neonatal resuscitation when maternal opioids have been given.

questions.q: The peak action of syntocinon administered to prevent postpartum haemorrhage is felt in
questions.explanation: Peak uterine effect of intramuscular oxytocin is approximately 2 minutes.

questions.q: Some of the health issues classified under the high priority health package in Kenya are
options: Mental health, control of vector-borne diseases
questions.explanation: Kenya’s high-priority package includes reproductive health and malaria prevention among others.

questions.q: When making an individual birth plan, the mother should consider
questions.explanation: Individual birth plan: birth companion, transport and place of delivery.

questions.q: In the treatment of tuberculosis, optic nerve is damaged by
questions.explanation: Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis.

questions.q: Some primary healthcare elements added by the Kenyan government include
options: Mental health, dental health, STI and HIV/AIDS control
Mental health, dental health, HIV/AIDS control, community rehabilitation, safe water supply
Nutrition and food supply, safe water supply, endemic disease control
Health education and essential drug supply
questions.explanation: Kenya added mental health, dental health, STI/HIV control (and others) to the classic PHC elements.

questions.q: Clients with gestational diabetes are usually managed by;
questions.explanation: Gestational diabetes is primarily managed with diet and exercise; insulin if targets not met (oral agents limited in pregnancy).

questions.q: A client is receiving MgSO₄ for severe PET. The adverse effect is;
questions.explanation: Magnesium toxicity: decreased urine output, respiratory depression, loss of reflexes.

questions.q: MgSO₄ toxicity with low urine output and respiratory depression is treated with;
questions.explanation: Calcium gluconate is the antidote for magnesium sulphate toxicity.

questions.q: Antidote for heparin is;
questions.explanation: Protamine sulphate is the antidote for heparin.

questions.q: Flat affect means;
questions.explanation: Flat affect = absence of facial emotional expression.

questions.q: Drugs for Ménière’s disease include;
questions.explanation: Ménière’s disease is managed with antiemetics, diuretics and sometimes antihistamines/steroids.

questions.q: Mefloquine prophylaxis is started;
questions.explanation: Mefloquine prophylaxis is started 2–3 weeks before travel in many regimens (some sources 1–2 weeks); exact timing follows current product guidance.

questions.q: Emergency contraception works within;
questions.explanation: Levonorgestrel emergency contraception is most effective within 72 hours (ulipristal up to 120 hours).

questions.q: To help a woman recognize the best time for conceiving a nurse would instruct the woman to monitor for
options: Increase in clear, stretchy cervical mucus
Drop in body temperature lasting several days
Breast tenderness with slight nipple discharge
questions.explanation: Peak fertility is associated with abundant clear, stretchy (spinnbarkeit) cervical mucus around ovulation.

questions.q: The following are clinical types of poliomyelitis i) Flaccid poliomyelitis ii) Abortive poliomyelitis iii) Non-abortive poliomyelitis iv) Non-paralytic poliomyelitis
questions.explanation: Clinical types of poliomyelitis include abortive, non-paralytic and paralytic (flaccid). 'Non-abortive' is not a standard category.

questions.q: The following are examples of “spacing methods” of family planning
options: Chemical barriers, natural methods, mechanical barriers
questions.explanation: Spacing methods are temporary: natural methods, chemical and mechanical barriers. Tubal ligation and vasectomy are permanent limiting methods.

questions.q: In environmental health, water based diseases are
options: Caused by vectors that live near aquatic conditions
Due to the presence of an aquatic host
Caused by poor quality of water
Due to inadequate quantities of water
questions.explanation: Water-based diseases require an aquatic intermediate host (e.g. schistosomiasis, guinea-worm). Water-washed = scarcity/hygiene; water-borne = contaminated water.

questions.q: In determination of disease incidence
options: The ability of disease to recur is not considered
All individuals suffering from the disease are considered
questions.explanation: Incidence rate uses person-time (person-years at risk) in the denominator.

questions.q: In descriptive epidemiology the important characteristics of study are
questions.explanation: Descriptive epidemiology characterises disease by person, place and time (demographic and related data).

questions.q: To effectively combat endemic malaria, health workers should
options: Distribute IT mosquito nets and intensify health education
Give more chemoprophylaxis and treat all cases
Provide mosquito nets and clear vegetation
questions.explanation: Core malaria control: insecticide-treated nets plus health education; case management and larval control are complementary.

questions.q: Nordette is an example of
questions.explanation: Nordette is a monophasic low-dose combined oral contraceptive.

questions.q: The scientific name for ringworm of the scalp is
questions.explanation: Tinea capitis = ringworm of the scalp.

questions.q: The vector that carries the causative organism for trypanosomiasis is
questions.explanation: Tsetse fly transmits Trypanosoma (sleeping sickness).

questions.q: The measures that would appropriately improve the health of the elderly include
options: Home safety programs, home based services
questions.explanation: Priority interventions for the elderly include home safety and home-based support services.

questions.q: Prevalence rate is defined as the number of
options: Old and new cases of a specified disease existing at a given time
New cases of a disease in a population over a period of time
Old cases of a specified disease existing at a given time
Deaths from a specified disease at a given time
questions.explanation: Prevalence = all existing (old + new) cases at a point or period in time.

questions.q: The demographic parameters the community health nurse will examine while conducting a community diagnosis include
questions.explanation: Community diagnosis examines demographic distribution and morbidity (among other health indicators).

questions.q: Vector borne diseases include
questions.explanation: Plague (flea) and leishmaniasis (sandfly) are vector-borne. Rubella is airborne/droplet; dysentery mainly faecal–oral.

questions.q: The follicle stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone are secreted by the
questions.explanation: FSH and LH are secreted by the anterior pituitary.

questions.q: The occupational disease that would occur in workers employed in a sugar cane factory is
questions.explanation: Bagassosis is hypersensitivity pneumonitis from mouldy sugar-cane bagasse.

questions.q: The measurement rate that is used to determine the number of new cases of a disease over an interval of time is
questions.explanation: Incidence rate measures new cases over a defined interval.

questions.q: The term used to describe malaria endemicity patterns where transmission occurs all year round is
questions.explanation: Holoendemic malaria = intense year-round transmission with high prevalence in children.

questions.q: The fungal skin infection characterized by thickening and discoloration of nails is called
questions.explanation: Tinea unguium (onychomycosis) affects the nails.

questions.q: The infection of the genital tract where the discharge has a fishy or ammonia odour is
questions.explanation: Trichomoniasis classically produces a frothy discharge with fishy/ammoniacal odour.

questions.q: A zoonotic disease that is caused by a spore-forming bacillus is
questions.explanation: Anthrax is caused by spore-forming Bacillus anthracis (zoonosis).

questions.q: The statistical measurement that takes into account all scores and shows the exact position of every score relative to the mean is
questions.explanation: Standard deviation incorporates every score and describes spread around the mean.

questions.q: Biphasic pills include
questions.explanation: Ovanon and Normovlar are biphasic pills.

questions.q: Following vasectomy procedure, the client should be advised to use condoms or another method for a duration of
questions.explanation: After vasectomy alternative contraception is advised for about 3 months (or until azoospermia confirmed).

questions.q: Water-washed diseases include
questions.explanation: Water-washed diseases (scabies, trachoma) are related to inadequate water for hygiene.

questions.q: Increasing the ability of the population to cope with a disaster is known as
questions.explanation: Preparedness = increasing capacity to cope with a disaster before it occurs.

questions.q: The oblique diameter of the pelvic brim is a line
options: From one sacro-iliac joint to the iliopectineal eminence
From the sacro-promontory to the upper border of the symphysis pubis
Between the points furthest apart on the iliopectineal lines
questions.explanation: Oblique diameter of the brim runs from one sacro-iliac joint to the opposite iliopectineal eminence.

questions.q: Internationally notifiable communicable diseases in Kenya include
questions.explanation: Internationally notifiable diseases in Kenya include yellow fever, cholera and plague.

questions.q: Tertiary prevention of diseases can best be described as
options: Preventing disability and maximizing use of remaining capacity
Treatment and isolation of the sick
Recovery from physical limitations and psychological regression
questions.explanation: Tertiary prevention aims to limit disability and maximise remaining function.

questions.q: Community Health Survey can be conducted to
options: Get a picture of the health and social status of the community
Plan the health programs of the community
Evaluate the community members to brief them of the program
questions.explanation: Community health surveys provide a picture of health and social status.

questions.q: A comprehensive school healthcare service includes
questions.explanation: Comprehensive school health includes surveillance among other components.

questions.q: The principal reason for providing occupational health services is for
questions.explanation: Occupational health services exist primarily for economic/efficiency reasons (healthy workforce) as well as protection.

questions.q: Herd immunity exists when;
options: Both live and dead vaccines are used
questions.explanation: Herd immunity exists when a high proportion of the population is immune, protecting the non-immune.

questions.q: Thought broadcasting diagnosis is;
questions.explanation: Thought broadcasting is a disturbance of thought process.

questions.q: The sign that leads a nurse to suspect apnoea in a two-week-old premature infant is
options: Lapse of spontaneous breathing for 20 seconds
questions.explanation: Apnoea of prematurity is defined as cessation of breathing ≥20 seconds (or shorter with bradycardia/cyanosis).

questions.q: A child with marasmus will present with the following clinical symptoms
options: Oedema of the legs but not the face
questions.explanation: Marasmus: severe wasting, poor appetite, no oedema. Kwashiorkor has oedema and often fatty liver.

questions.q: The demographic trends in Kenya indicate that since 1969 to date
options: The crude birth rate has increased
The infant mortality rate has increased
Life expectancy at birth has increased
questions.explanation: Since 1969 Kenya has seen rising life expectancy and falling infant mortality and fertility rates; crude birth rate has declined.

questions.q: A child growing within normal developmental milestones will be able to walk at the age of
questions.explanation: Independent walking is expected between 12 and 18 months.

questions.q: The approximate calorie needs for young children under five years are
questions.explanation: Approximate energy requirement for children under five is about 100 kcal/kg/day.

questions.q: Some of the developmental tasks of a beginning family are
options: Relating to kin network, maintaining a stable marriage
Family planning, relating to kin network
Family planning, stabilizing the family unit
Stabilizing the family unit, socializing children
questions.explanation: Beginning (couple) family developmental tasks: establish marriage, relate to kin network.

questions.q: Post obstetric history includes i) Any abnormality during previous pregnancies, labour and puerperium ii) Age at menarche iii) History of twinning in the family iv) Miscarriages and gestation when they occurred v) Number of children with ages and birth weight
questions.explanation: Past obstetric history includes previous pregnancy/labour/puerperium abnormalities, family history of twinning, and details of previous children (ages, weights). Age at menarche belongs to menstrual history.

questions.q: The age at which a child is likely to conceptualize abstract ideas is
questions.explanation: Abstract thought typically emerges around 11–12 years (formal operational stage).

questions.q: The neonate loses heat instantly at birth because of
questions.explanation: Large surface-area-to-mass ratio is the main reason neonates lose heat rapidly.

questions.q: Highest priority in neonatal temperature regulation is;
options: Prevent heat loss (radiation, convection, conduction, evaporation)
questions.explanation: Priority is prevention of heat loss by all four mechanisms (radiation, convection, conduction, evaporation).

questions.q: A woman complains of morning sickness during the first trimester. To alleviate symptoms she should
questions.explanation: Avoiding strong odours reduces nausea triggers. Small frequent meals and avoiding empty stomach are also advised; low-protein or clear-liquid diets are not recommended.

questions.q: The first scientific paper in nursing was published by
questions.explanation: Florence Nightingale’s work (including Notes on Nursing and Crimean War statistics) is regarded as the first scientific nursing publication.

questions.q: The components of the biological environment include
questions.explanation: Biological environment includes living elements that affect health: food, water supplies, microorganisms, etc.

questions.q: A behavior therapy technique used in treatment of sexual aversion disorder is
questions.explanation: Systematic desensitization is a behaviour-therapy technique used for sexual aversion and phobias.

questions.q: Family descent where membership is acquired through the male line is
questions.explanation: Patrilineal descent is traced through the male line.

questions.q: The home visiting phase where the nurse designs a plan of action for the family is
questions.explanation: In the pre-visit phase the nurse plans the home visit.

questions.q: The anteverted position of the uterus is maintained by
questions.explanation: The round ligaments help maintain anteversion of the uterus.

questions.q: The stage of an eclamptic fit where muscles become rigid, teeth clenched and eyes staring is
questions.explanation: Tonic phase of an eclamptic fit: generalised rigidity, clenched teeth, staring eyes.

questions.q: Sequential steps in family health care plan is
options: Statement of problem, objectives, intervention and evaluation
Evaluation, statement of problems, objectives and interventions
Objectives, evaluation, evaluation and statement of problems
Objectives, statement of problem, interventions and evaluation
questions.explanation: Family care plan sequence: problem statement → objectives → interventions → evaluation.

questions.q: Virulence can best be defined as
options: Degree of pathogenicity of an infective agent
Disease caused by a viral agent
Capability of an agent to cause disease in a susceptible host
Disease due to toxic products from infective agent
questions.explanation: Virulence = degree of pathogenicity of an agent.

questions.q: The graduate nurse’s role in research is
questions.explanation: The graduate nurse’s primary research role is intelligent consumption and application of findings; conducting independent research usually requires further training.

questions.q: A nurse researcher formulated the following hypothesis: “There is a relationship between self-concept and suicidal behavior”. This implies that
options: The dependent variable is suicidal behavior
The independent variable is suicidal behavior
The type of design suggested would be experimental
questions.explanation: In the hypothesis, suicidal behaviour is the dependent (outcome) variable; self-concept is independent. The hypothesis is non-directional.

questions.q: Theoretical framework refers to
options: An examination of both the depth and breadth of literature review
A pictorial presentation of relationships between variables
A comprehensive list of all relevant previous research work in an area of interest
questions.explanation: A theoretical/conceptual framework is often presented as a diagram showing relationships among variables.

questions.q: The main purpose of publishing research findings is to
options: Solicit for more funds for future research
Meet the requirements of the sponsor
questions.explanation: Conservative management of varicose veins in pregnancy: support stockings/crepe, leg elevation, avoid prolonged standing.

questions.q: It is difficult to obtain meaningful informed consent in qualitative research because the researcher does not know in advance how the study will evolve. This kind of consent is called
questions.explanation: In evolving qualitative designs, process (ongoing) consent is used because the study path is not fully known in advance.

questions.q: When an assessment tool measures what it is supposed to measure, it is said to have
questions.explanation: Validity = the instrument measures what it is intended to measure.

questions.q: A research instrument that gives the same measurements when repeated several times is said to be
questions.explanation: Reliability = consistency of measurement on repeated testing.

questions.q: The hypothesis that rivals the null hypothesis is referred to as
questions.explanation: The alternative hypothesis is the rival to the null hypothesis.

questions.q: A research design which provides the strongest evidence about cause and effect relationship is
questions.explanation: True experimental designs provide the strongest evidence for causality.
